messages:
morgan: Heads up — after the kernel-prefetch canary yesterday we see p95 regressions on chat routes. Not huge, but noticeable for tier=standard. :thinking:
alan: Which metric are you looking at? p95 tokens/latency or end-to-end?
jyoti: I pulled the profiler traces for the 11:30–12:00 window. Root cause looks like increased KV cache misses + microbatch churn after the token-budget gating landed.
morgan: exact numbers: baseline p95 ~82ms, after change p95 ~148ms on chat.default (seq avg ~128). Throughput stable. KV hit-rate dropped from 84% -> 61% for that route.
sam: Oof. That aligns with the batcher forming smaller microbatches because budget gating returned lower token budgets for standard tier. Fewer shared prefixes -> worse KV locality.
alan: Any kernel switch flapping? I remember we also toggled kernel-selection heuristic (prefetch threshold) in the same canary.
jyoti: yes, kernel switch count jumped ~2.4x. Overhead per switch ~1.8ms avg — not enough to explain full p95 but adds up when batches are small.
morgan: here's the route config we rolled out (simplified):
```
route: chat.default
priority: standard
token_budget_target: dynamic
budget_by_tier:
  enterprise: 1200
  standard: 600 -> auto-sculpt (recent patch)
prefetch_threshold: 0.65 -> 0.5 (canary)
queue_policy: slo_aware
```
alan: Proposal: revert the auto-sculpt for standard tier back to static 700 and keep the prefetch_threshold at 0.65, then ramp the dynamic budget with a gentler slope.
jyoti: Agreed. Also we should try a quick experiment: keep dynamic budgets but increase the KV retention window for standard tier caching from 45s -> 120s to reduce churn.
morgan: Can we run a 2-hour canary on 10% of standard traffic with these two changes? I can trigger the rollout. :thumbsup:
sam: I'll add a microbatching trace and enable kernel-switch debug for the canary. If we see switch flapping >1.5x baseline or KV hit-rate <70% we auto-rollback.
perf-bot: experiment scheduled: canary_id=canary-2026-03-18-rc3, target=10%, start=5043220400, rollback_condition=(kv_hit<0.70 OR kernel_switch_rate>1.5x OR p95>1.3x baseline)
alan: Also add a metric for "avg microbatch size at tail" — we care about p95 spikes caused by many tiny batches.
jyoti: I've attached a shortened trace dump in the incident board (link) and a small script to compute microbatch histograms: `scripts/mb_hist.py --route chat.default --window 30m`.
morgan: plan sounds good. I'll schedule the canary and loop back with results in ~3hrs. If we still see >120ms p95, we escalate to kernel/runtime.
alan: thanks — thanks for the quick triage everyone. :eyes:
